numeric_complexity_contract.reference: keep a dictionary of pattern to handler and, per query, test every pattern of the right length and keep the best (wildcard count, wildcard positions) key
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: segment trie whose children are literal segments plus one "*" child; a query walks the trie depth first, literal child before "*", carrying the wildcard count, pruning branches whose count already exceeds the best complete match, and keeps the first best match found in that order
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(min(T, 2^L)) per call worst case, T = trie nodes, L = path segments; O(L) per addRoute/O(total pattern segments) space

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: quadratic dynamic programme over the last chosen index and the number of changes used so far, trying every earlier index as the predecessor
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: dynamic programme keyed by value: best[v][j] is the longest subsequence ending in value v with j changes, and top[j] the best over all values; each element extends best[v][j] by one or starts a new run after top[j - 1], updating j from k down to 0
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(n * k) time/O(d * k) space, d = distinct values

numeric_complexity_contract.reference: bottom-up dynamic programming table over prefixes of s and p
numeric_complexity_contract.candidate_design: split p at "*" into literal pieces; the first piece must be a prefix of s and the last a suffix (when p has a "*"), and each middle piece is placed at its leftmost occurrence after the previous one, which is optimal because "*" absorbs any gap
numeric_complexity_contract.complexity_target: O(|s| * |p|) worst case with a linear substring search, usually near linear/O(|p|) space
